scenario: a community forum tracking thread participation and member retention
title: Forum Thread Engagement by Category
prompt: You are analyzing a community forum system modeled on public forum engagement datasets (Discourse, Stack Overflow public data dumps). The `threads` table stores discussion topics with their category and creation date. The `posts` table records each reply with a member identifier and post timestamp. Your task is to identify categories with strong engagement: categories where the total reply count is at least 8 posts AND where at least one thread has received 3 or more replies. For each qualifying category, report the category name (cleaned and capitalized), the total reply count across all threads in that category, the maximum number of replies any single thread received, the tags array's first element, the month number when the earliest thread in that category was created, and a tier label. The tier is 'premium' if the total reply count is 15 or more, otherwise 'standard'. Some categories may have NULL tags or missing data. Order results by total reply count descending, then by category name ascending.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE threads (thread_id INT PRIMARY KEY, category VARCHAR(100), created_at DATE, tags TEXT[]); CREATE TABLE posts (post_id INT PRIMARY KEY, thread_id INT, member_id INT, posted_at TIMESTAMP);
answer_key: WITH thread_replies AS (SELECT t.thread_id, INITCAP(TRIM(t.category)) AS category_name, t.created_at, t.tags, COUNT(p.post_id) AS reply_count FROM threads t LEFT JOIN posts p ON t.thread_id = p.thread_id GROUP BY t.thread_id, t.category, t.created_at, t.tags), category_agg AS (SELECT category_name, SUM(reply_count) AS total_replies, GREATEST(MAX(reply_count), 0) AS max_thread_replies, MIN(created_at) AS earliest_created, (ARRAY_AGG(tags[1]) FILTER (WHERE tags IS NOT NULL AND ARRAY_LENGTH(tags, 1) > 0))[1] AS primary_tag FROM thread_replies GROUP BY category_name HAVING SUM(reply_count) >= 8 AND GREATEST(MAX(reply_count), 0) >= 3) SELECT category_name, total_replies::NUMERIC AS total_replies, max_thread_replies, primary_tag, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM earliest_created)::INT AS creation_month, CASE WHEN COALESCE(total_replies, 0) >= 15 THEN 'premium' ELSE 'standard' END AS engagement_tier FROM category_agg ORDER BY total_replies DESC, category_name ASC;
user_solution:
/*


*/

WITH max_tread AS (
    SELECT
        t.thread_id,
        COUNT(*) AS thread_replies
    FROM posts AS p
    JOIN threads AS t
    ON p.thread_id = t.thread_id
    GROUP BY t.thread_id
),
earliest_tag AS (
    SELECT
        INITCAP(TRIM(t.category)) AS category_name,
        LOWER(TRIM(tags[1])) AS primary_tag,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY INITCAP(TRIM(t.category)) ORDER BY created_at::date) AS rn
    FROM threads AS t
)
SELECT
    INITCAP(TRIM(t.category)) AS category_name,
    COALESCE(COUNT(p.post_id),0) AS total_replies,
    MAX(m.thread_replies) AS max_thread_replies,
    MAX(e.primary_tag) AS primary_tag,
    MIN(EXTRACT(month FROM t.created_at)) AS creation_month,
    CASE WHEN COALESCE(COUNT(p.post_id),0) >= 15 THEN 'premium' ELSE  'standard' END AS engagement_tier
FROM posts AS p
JOIN threads AS t
    ON p.thread_id = t.thread_id
JOIN max_tread AS m
    ON p.thread_id = m.thread_id
JOIN earliest_tag AS e
    ON INITCAP(TRIM(t.category)) = e.category_name
WHERE e.rn = 1
GROUP BY t.category
HAVING COALESCE(COUNT(p.post_id),0) >= 8 AND MAX(m.thread_replies) >= 3
ORDER BY total_replies DESC, category_name;
